newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia 1Qtr GDP growth at 8.2 pct - Negara.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia 1Qtr GDP growth at 8.2 pct - Negara.

text.p: Malaysia's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth in the first quarter of 1997 was 8.2 percent against 8.3 percent in the same period last year, the Bank Negara said on Friday.
In its quarterly report on the economy, the central bank said output in the manufacturing sector grew by 12.9 percent.

Manufacturing growth in the year-ago first quarter was 14.0 percent. Bank Negara said output from the electronics industry in the first quarter of 1997 expanded by 22.9 percent, "reflecting an improvement in the global demand for semiconductors".

Other industries recording strong growth were chemicals and chemical products (22.6 percent), fabricated metal products (17.4 percent), transport equipment (13.6 percent) and construction-related products (13.2 percent).

The services sector expanded by 9.0 percent against 8.7 in the same comparative period last year. Among sectors recording growth were electricity, gas and water; transport, as well as storage and communications.

Construction grew 14.0 percent in the first quarter against 11 percent in the 1996 period, "with the continued implementation of large infrastructure and civil engineering projects" as well as sustained activity in residential and non-residential construction, the statement said.

The net international reserves held by Bank Negara rose by 2.1 billion ringgit during the first quarter to 72.2 billion ringgit at the end of March, sufficient to finance about 4.7 months of retained imports.
At May 15, external reserves fell to 71.1 billion ringgit, as a result of short-term capital outflow as the stock market consolidated during the first quarter.
Lending by the banking system for consumption purposes stood at 28.4 percent at the end of March versus 35.7 percent at the end of December 1996.

Loans to the manufacturing and property sectors rose at annual rates of 13 percent and 29.2 percent, respectively, at the end of March, compared with 14 percent and 26.8 percent, respectively at the end of the similar 1996 period.
